expectations.text: Batches the interview questions before designing: agent audience, release mechanism and license, existing skills including the community one, deadline and effort ceiling, and whether the package may gain a console command.
expectations.evidence: Only four confirmations (arg order, pyproject, tags, license); no audience, community skill, deadline or console command questions.

expectations.text: Keeps the default rungs because of the near deadline, deferring the starved options (bundled install command, golden agent tasks).
expectations.evidence: 'Not this week: an MCP server, a bundled rushmere skills install subcommand'; gate 5 deferred

expectations.text: Turns the three named failures (swapped arguments, rushmere.legacy import, strict=False) into the skill's first content and its tests.
expectations.evidence: Skill sections for arg order, strict, rushmere.legacy; dry-run test for legacy

expectations.text: Places the skill at skills/rushmere/SKILL.md at the repo root and includes skills/ as package data so the wheel carries it.
expectations.evidence: Checks sdist; wheel inclusion only 'if you want it there'.

expectations.text: Makes pyproject.toml the version source of truth, bumps metadata.version and the Skill version body line in the release commit, and adds a check that the tag equals the pyproject version.
expectations.evidence: 'Tag equals pyproject version' step; --write bumps both version spots

expectations.text: Runs scripts/check-skill-version.py on pull requests against the pyproject version and on the tag as a backstop.
expectations.evidence: Workflow runs on pull_request and is called from the tag workflow

expectations.text: Adds the library content check: `python -m py_compile` plus an import smoke test on every extracted code block against the release build.
expectations.evidence: AST-based import and signature check of python fences against the installed wheel

expectations.text: Opens the body with a library guard that reads the installed version (`pip show rushmere`) and prefers bundled docs when major or minor differs.
expectations.evidence: 'python -c "import importlib.metadata... m.version('rushmere')"' with two-sided branches

expectations.text: Handles the community skill by publishing under the project's own namespace and claiming obvious name variants, because agents hallucinate skill names and attackers register them.
expectations.evidence: Ships under same name and opens an issue, but doesn't claim name variants.

expectations.text: Sets license to the repo's license and writes the description as what plus when, with the tool's name and the tasks users type.
expectations.evidence: Draft uses 'license: MIT' as an assumption, though told to replace.
